name: Simple Steps for Installing Your New Showerhead

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Putting in a new showerhead, whether it’s a standard adjustable one or a handheld unit, is a pretty common DIY task. But to make sure it works perfectly and doesn't leak, following a few simple steps makes all the difference.

step.name: Step 2
step.text: **Step 1: Remove the Old Showerhead.** Grab a wrench (if needed, but often hand-loosening works) and twist off your old showerhead. Be careful not to damage the shower arm.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: **Step 2: Clean the Threads.** This is super important! Make sure there's no old thread tape residue or mineral buildup on the shower arm threads. A clean surface ensures a good seal for your new unit.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: **Step 3: Apply the Right Seal.** Check your new showerhead's instructions. Some units need new thread seal tape wrapped clockwise around the shower arm threads. Others rely on a rubber washer inside the showerhead or bracket. For handheld units, make sure any included diverter or bracket is installed correctly here with its seals.

step.name: Step 5
step.text: **Step 4: Install the New Showerhead.** Carefully screw on your new showerhead (or the bracket for a handheld). Hand-tighten it first, and only use a wrench gently if the instructions say so and it’s still loose. Overtightening is a common mistake! For handhelds, connect the hose, making sure any washers are in place and the vacuum breaker (if included) is oriented correctly.

step.name: Step 6
step.text: **Step 5: Test for Leaks and Functionality.** Turn on the water and check thoroughly for any drips. If it's an adjustable showerhead, cycle through all the spray settings to ensure they work. If you're still seeing leaks, have very low flow, or if your installation needs more complex plumbing changes, don't hesitate to call a pro like HH Remodeling LLC.
